rules.statement: A will can create a valid fideicommissum even if the fiduciary does not have personal benefit from the property.
rules.supporting_quote: "The possibility of a fiduciary burdened with administrative duties, without having any rights of enjoyment for himself, seems to have sprung from obiter dicta of de Villiers C. J., (afterwards Lord Villiers) in Strydom v. Strydom's Trustee (1894) 11 S. C. 425, which were based upon a mistranslation of D. 36. 2.26.1 ( recording what is called Papinian's case)."
